TRREB.kpis: The GTA is sitting in balanced territory this month at 4.8 months of inventory, and the most useful message for your clients is that neither side holds a clear edge. Average price came in at $993,410, down 1.1% from July and down 2.7% year over year, so pricing conversations should center on realistic expectations rather than momentum in either direction.
TRREB.price: With the average at $993,410 down three months in a row and the median at $850,000 down 4.2% year over year, tell your sellers that aggressive asking prices are meeting resistance. Frame offers for your buyers around recent solds, because the softening gives them room to negotiate without expecting steep discounts.
TRREB.balance: An SNLR of 37.5%, up 0.4 points and now rising seven months straight, points to demand slowly catching up to supply even as the market stays balanced. At the table, remind clients that leverage is close to even, so terms and conditions carry as much weight as price in getting a deal across.
TRREB.activity: Sales of 5,057 slipped 2.1% while new listings fell 14.1% and active inventory dropped 11.3%, so the pool of choices is thinning. With 51 days on market and a 97% sale to list ratio, coach your buyers to move deliberately on well priced homes and your sellers to price sharp from day one.

Halton.kpis: Halton is balanced at 4.2 months of inventory, but the numbers show a market cooling on the seller side. Average price of $1,110,436 fell 3.6% month over month and 4.2% year over year, so the clearest thing to tell clients is that patience and precise pricing matter more here than a year ago.
Halton.price: The median at $957,000 is down 6.1% year over year, and with the average posting its third straight monthly decline, your sellers need to hear that last year's comparables no longer apply. Buyers should be encouraged to anchor offers to current data, where the softer trend gives them a stronger footing.
Halton.balance: SNLR of 40.0% ticked up 0.5 points and has climbed seven months running, while months of inventory has risen three months in a row. That combination keeps things balanced but tilting slightly toward buyers, so at the table your buyers can push on price and conditions with more confidence.
Halton.activity: Sales of 571 dropped 10.2% and new listings fell 24.7%, a sharp pullback in fresh supply that active listings, down 17.3%, partly reflects. With 57 days on market and a 96% sale to list ratio, tell your sellers that overpricing extends time on market, and buyers have breathing room to inspect before committing.

Peel.kpis: Peel holds a balanced market at 5.0 months of inventory, and it stands out as the region where sales actually grew. Average price of $908,415 was essentially flat month over month at down 0.2% but down 5.2% year over year, so tell clients demand is steady while values remain below last year.
Peel.price: With the average nearly unchanged from July and the median at $850,000 down 4.5% year over year, the pricing story here is stability after a longer decline. Advise your sellers that the month over month steadiness supports a fair asking price, and let buyers know the year over year gap is where their leverage sits.
Peel.balance: An SNLR of 34.8%, up 0.8 points and rising seven months in a row, is the strongest monthly gain among the core regions and signals demand firming against supply. Balance still holds, so at the negotiating table remind clients that neither party can dictate terms outright.
Peel.activity: Sales rose 4.7% to 940 even as new listings fell 22.7% and active inventory dropped 14.8%, a tightening backdrop that supports pricing. With 55 days on market and a 97% sale to list ratio, coach your buyers not to assume deep discounts and your sellers that reasonable pricing is finding takers.

Toronto.kpis: Toronto is balanced at 4.9 months of inventory, and the headline for your clients is resilience underneath a monthly dip. Average price of $979,684 fell 3.1% from July but is down only 1.1% year over year, the shallowest annual decline among the larger regions, so the market here is holding firmer than the monthly figure suggests.
Toronto.price: The median at $770,000 is down 3.7% year over year while the average posts its third consecutive monthly decline. Tell your sellers the annual softness is modest, so they need not chase the market down, and remind buyers that the month over month move offers a near term opening on well priced listings.
Toronto.balance: SNLR of 38.3% edged up 0.2 points and has risen seven months straight, keeping the market balanced with demand gradually strengthening. At the table, that near even footing means your clients should weigh closing flexibility and conditions alongside price rather than expecting one side to concede.
Toronto.activity: Sales of 1,767 were essentially flat at down 0.2% while new listings fell 7.4% and active inventory dropped 9.8%. At 46 days on market, the fastest pace among the regions, with a 97% sale to list ratio, tell your buyers that sharp listings move quickly and your sellers that correct pricing still draws prompt attention.
